Our philosophy

We focus on sensory precision and somatic safety. Sessions are designed to be accessible: low lights, comfortable temperature, and carefully considered instrument timbre to avoid overstimulation while encouraging deep rest.

Facilitator

{{FACILITATOR_NAME}} blends clinical training with decades of live sound work. Their approach is measured, trauma-aware, and informed by physiology.

Signature instruments

  • Crystal singing bowls tuned to whole-body resonances
  • Himalayan-style gong for long-form overtone wash
  • Koshi and wind chimes for gentle, high-frequency articulation

Each event's instrumentation is selected to cultivate safety-first immersion; the combination varies by intent and space acoustics.

What people experience

Participants commonly report slowed breathing, reduced muscle tension, clearer thinking afterward, and a heightened sense of presence. Experiences vary; all sessions are non-psychotherapeutic and meant as supportive wellness practices.

Plan your visit

We host events at {{VENUE_NAME}} in {{CITY}}, {{STATE}}. The space is accessible and climate-controlled; street parking and transit options are available nearby.

What to bring

  • Yoga mat or blanket to lie on
  • A pillow and light covering for comfort
  • Optional eye mask and water bottle

Contraindications (clinical note)

Sound baths are generally safe, but please avoid participation if you have uncontrolled epilepsy, recent head trauma, or severe auditory hypersensitivity. If pregnant, use discretion and consult your care provider. For implants or medical devices, check with your clinician. If in doubt, contact us at {{EMAIL}} before booking.

Community care and accessibility

We offer limited low-sensory seating and a small number of full-reimbursement seats for those with financial need when available. Please email {{EMAIL}} with requests at least 72 hours prior.

Frequently Asked — {{BUSINESS_NAME}}

Concise, clinical clarity for participants
Back Events Reserve

Common questions

What is a sound bath and how does it help?
A sound bath is a guided session where resonant instruments create a sustained sonic environment. The focused tones help shift attention away from worry and toward interoception — often producing lowered heart rate and increased parasympathetic activity. Sessions are supportive, non-diagnostic, and intended for wellbeing.
How long should I expect the session to be?
Typical group events last 60–80 minutes in total (settling, sound, and re-orientation). Private sessions may be scheduled for 45–120 minutes depending on goals.
What should I bring?
Bring a comfortable mat or blanket, pillow, and a light cover. Avoid heavy scents. Earplugs are welcome if you prefer reduced intensity. Hydrate before and after.
Contraindications and safety
Do not attend if you have uncontrolled seizures, recent traumatic brain injury, or severe sound sensitivity. If you have implanted devices, pacemakers, or are in advanced pregnancy, consult a clinician first. We cannot provide medical advice; contact your provider for individual clearance. For event-specific concerns email {{EMAIL}}.
Are sessions suitable for first-timers?
Yes. Facilitators will give brief orientation. You may rest, sit, or leave at any time. There is no required practice level.
Do you use the same instruments each time?
We curate instrument palettes intentionally. Examples we rotate: tuning forks and monochord for precise frequency work, rainstick for grounding textures, and tempered bell tones for articulation. Each event's mix is chosen for its therapeutic intent.
Payment and cancellations
Bookings are confirmed at time of payment. Refunds available up to 72 hours before event; after that we offer credit for a future event when possible. For private sessions please see our booking page or contact {{EMAIL}}.

Session flow (brief)

  1. Arrival & intention setting
  2. Guided breath and body-scan
  3. Sonic journey with gradual dynamic arcs
  4. Soft return and optional check-in

If you hear tones differently

Some people notice ringing or phasing for hours after — this is usually benign but if it persists, seek medical guidance. Bring earplugs if you know you are sensitive.

Accessibility

We prioritize clear access. Please share mobility, sensory, or other needs at {{EMAIL}} at least 48 hours before your visit so we can prepare suitable seating and entry support.

Private sessions

Private offerings include 1:1 clinical-style sessions, couples sessions, and corporate soundings focused on group regulation. See 'Sessions' page for details or contact {{EMAIL}} to discuss a tailored plan.
